Why do tomatoes turn green when they unripen?
Not sure if the two are similar processes, but I would think it is related to the process leaves go through when they change color.

Chlorophyll is very important to plants. Without it, they can't breathe out waste products. When tomatoes unripen (by moving in a negative direction on the t-axis) they have more chlorophyll because they are breathing negatively (outwards). You can also see this in related fruits, like bananas, algae, and people who get seasick. More green = more coming out.
